prayerExcerpt.en-US: A Christian ought to be afraid of no enemy more than himself, whom he carries always about with him, and from whom he is not able to flee.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Um cristão não deve temer nenhum inimigo mais do que a si mesmo, a quem carrega sempre consigo, e de quem não é capaz de fugir.

meta.face: A Roman of about sixty-five with a warm, light-olive complexion and a ROUND, FIRM face as WIDE as it is long — not fleshy: a ROUND, bald crown ringed at the sides and back by short, CRISP, curly grey hair, a broad, smooth forehead crossed by ONE deep vertical FROWN LINE between the brows, FIRM, apple-round cheekbones, a SHORT, straight nose with a HIGH, narrow bridge, SMALL, keen, DEEP-SET dark-brown eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT, dark-grey brows, deep lines running from the nose to the corners of a small, firm, closed mouth; a SHORT, crisp, curly grey beard following the round line of the jaw to a blunt point; the gaze level, alert and watchful. Not the soft, round, mild-eyed gal_clermont, the flat-featured, flat-nosed zephyrinus, the curl-browed, protruding-eyed felix_i, the heavy-lidded, fleshy marcellinus_pope, or the long, narrow sylvester.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The medallion of St. Paul Outside the Walls (Italian Wikipedia's lead image) gives a broad, bearded face with curly hair, which the card keeps as a round, firm, watchful face; the basilica on the Via Ardeatina is the Martyrology's and the Liber Pontificalis's (via Wikipedia), and the book's engraving shows him among building stones.
